title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery

paragraphs.en: Reproducible and analytically robust research findings are essential to scientific progress, but evaluating these properties typically requires costly manual effort. We investigate whether LLM agents can help automate reproduction and robustness analysis, using a medical case study grounded in the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, a widely used U.S. cancer registry underlying tens of thousands of published studies. First, we introduce SEER-Repro , a benchmark of 20 published SEER-based papers together with the data and resources required to reproduce their findings. Second, we create an AI agent that successfully reproduces 77.4% of 2,190 atomic claims, while providing executable baselines for further analysis. Third, we develop an agentic analysis pipeline to test the robustness of the medical findings by identifying analytical choices underlying each finding, proposing defensible alternatives, and rerunning the analysis to determine whether those choices affect the conclusion. Across published papers in SEER-Repro, our pipeline identifies potentially consequential analytical choices in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings and flags them for expert review. These results show how LLM agents can support scientific review by reproducing findings, systematically testing their robustness, and directing expert attention toward potentially consequential analytical choices.

paragraphs.en: Reproducibility and analytical robustness are the bedrock on which scientific discovery rests. Reproducibility ensures that research findings can be independently verified, while analytical robustness asks whether conclusions remain stable under reasonable alternative choices. Traditionally, meta-analyses and systematic reviews have addressed these challenges through laborious, manual efforts to reproduce experiments or reanalyze data using alternate specifications ( Delios and others, 2022 ; Brodeur et al., 2026 ) . However, the immense cost and expertise required for such metascientific investigations have limited their scalability. Scientific claims also depend on the analytical decisions made by their authors ( Simonsohn et al., 2020 ; Bertran et al., 2026 ) . Recent “many-analyst” studies in psychology and the social sciences show that independent teams addressing the same hypothesis and dataset can reach conflicting conclusions ( Silberzahn et al., 2018 ; Breznau et al., 2022 ; Botvinik-Nezer et al., 2020 ) . Large language models (LLMs) offer a way to explore this analytical diversity at scale. Importantly, these AI-driven results exhibit notable steerability: shifting the design of the analyst persona or changing the underlying LLM meaningfully alters the distribution of analytic outcomes, even when methodological rigor is maintained throughout ( Bertran et al., 2026 ; Miao et al., 2026 ) .

paragraphs.en: Does this sensitivity to analytical choices documented in psychological and social sciences extend to medicine, where findings profoundly inform clinical decisions and patient care? Addressing this question is critical, as the validity of medical research underpins clinical decisions that affect countless lives. In this paper, we investigate the potential of AI-driven analysts to enhance both reproducibility and analytical robustness in scientific discovery, with a particular focus on medical epidemiology using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. Maintained by the National Cancer Institute since 1973, the program integrates population-based cancer-registry records on patient demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment, and survival. In its 2024 usage metrics, NCI reports that 17 core registries cover roughly 48% of the U.S. population and collect approximately 950,000 incident cases per year ( National Cancer Institute, 2026e ; National Cancer Institute, 2025 ) . From 1975 through 2024, approximately 25,000 publications used SEER data in their primary analysis, while more than 126,000 publications referenced SEER data ( National Cancer Institute, 2025 ) . This scale provides a large body of realistic, high-impact questions, while differences in data and analytical definitions, such as registry coverage and cohort selection, make faithful reconstruction challenging.
paragraphs.zh: 心理学和社会科学中记录的对分析选择的这种敏感性，是否也适用于医学领域？因为医学研究结果对临床决策和患者护理具有深远影响。 回答这个问题至关重要，因为医学研究的可靠性是支撑临床决策的基础，而这些决策影响着无数人的生命。 在本文中，我们探讨了由人工智能驱动的分析员在科学发现中提升可重复性和分析稳健性的潜力，特别聚焦于使用“监测、流行病学和最终结果”（SEER）数据库的医学流行病学领域。 自1973年以来，该项目一直由美国国家癌症研究所维护，整合了基于人群的癌症登记记录，涵盖患者人口统计学特征、肿瘤特性、治疗及生存情况。 在其2024年的使用指标中，美国国家癌症研究所报告称，17个核心登记系统覆盖了约48%的美国人口，每年收集约95万例新发病例（美国国家癌症研究所，2026e；美国国家癌症研究所，2025）。 从1975年到2024年，约有2.5万篇出版物在其主要分析中使用了SEER数据，而超过12.6万篇出版物引用了SEER数据（美国国家癌症研究所，2025）。 这一规模提供了大量真实且具有高度影响力的问题，但数据和定义上的差异——例如登记系统的覆盖范围和队列选择——使得忠实地重建研究过程变得困难。

paragraphs.en: Second, can we create an AI agent to evaluate the analytical robustness of findings in SEER-Repro? And if so, how robust are those findings to reasonable alternative analytical choices? We formulate the task of analytical robustness evaluation as follows: Given a research report and access to the underlying data, the task is to investigate if there are well-justified analytical choices that can change the conclusions of the report. We refer to such choices as consequential . Evaluating analytical robustness is challenging because gold-standard judgments do not exist. We therefore investigate three complementary approaches: (1) asking a coding agent to independently analyze the data and comparing its conclusions with those of the published paper; (2) systematically perturbing individual analytical choices through a structured agentic pipeline; and (3) asking coding agents to assess analytical robustness directly. To rate how strongly alternative analyses could change published conclusions, we adapted GRADE ( Guyatt et al., 2008 ) , an established framework for evaluating clinical evidence that rates the importance of outcomes on a nine-point scale, with scores of 7-9 indicating outcomes critical to decision-making.

sents.zh: 因此，我们研究了三种互补的方法：（1）让一个编码智能体独立分析数据，并将其结论与已发表论文中的结论进行比较；（2）通过结构化的智能体流程系统性地扰动各个分析选择；以及（3）直接要求编码智能体评估分析稳健性。

sents.en: To rate how strongly alternative analyses could change published conclusions, we adapted GRADE ( Guyatt et al., 2008 ) , an established framework for evaluating clinical evidence that rates the importance of outcomes on a nine-point scale, with scores of 7-9 indicating outcomes critical to decision-making.
sents.zh: 为了评价替代性分析在多大程度上可能改变已发表的结论，我们改用了 GRADE（Guyatt 等人，2008），这是一个用于评估临床证据的成熟框架，它通过九分制量表对结果的重要性进行评分，其中 7-9 分的分数表示这些结果对决策至关重要。

paragraphs.en: Our results show that major effects (scores 7–9) are flagged in 9.5% of fully reproduced findings (55 of 579). paragraphs.en: Deep-research benchmarks such as DeepResearchBench, ReportBench, and DeepScholar-Bench assess report quality, evidence coverage, and citation grounding ( Du et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Patel et al., 2025 ) . Data-oriented benchmarks evaluate insight generation and executable scientific workflows, including InsightBench, DiscoveryBench, and ScienceAgentBench ( Sahu et al., 2025 ; Majumder et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ) . BLADE additionally evaluates conceptual variables, transformations, and models across multiple valid analyses ( Gu et al., 2024 ) . DataSTORM, Hunt, and DAgent extend this setting to database investigation and report generation ( Liu et al., 2026a ; Liu et al., 2026b ; Xu et al., 2025 ) . Our evaluation asks whether a report’s conclusions survive defensible changes to the analytical choices that produced them, using executed alternatives linked to individual findings. This report-level assessment of analytical robustness is not covered by these prior benchmarks and evaluations.

paragraphs.en: Extract findings and atomic claims : First, we extract the empirical findings F p = { f 1 , … , f m } F_{p}=\{f_{1},\ldots,f_{m}\} . These findings represent the core contributions of the paper and underpin the conclusion it draws. We exclude sections of the paper pertaining to related work, background context, or methodology. Each finding f i f_{i} is then decomposed into a set of atomic claims A i = { a i ​ j } j = 1 n i A_{i}=\{a_{ij}\}_{j=1}^{n_{i}} . One atomic claim involves one specific numerical or qualitative target while one finding could group multiple atomic claims together. For instance, “Among women with adenoid cystic carcinoma of the breast, the mean age at diagnosis was 63 years, the median was 62 years, and the range was 33–97 years” is a finding, while its individual targets such as “Among women with adenoid cystic carcinoma of the breast, the mean age at diagnosis was 63 years” (and similarly for “median age: 62 years” and “age range: 33–97 years”) each become a separate atomic claim.
paragraphs.zh: 提取研究结果与原子性论断：首先，我们提取经验性研究结果 F p = { f 1 , … , f m } F_{p}=\{f_{1},\ldots,f_{m}\}。 这些研究结果构成了本文的核心贡献，并支撑了本文得出的结论。 我们不包含与相关工作、背景语境或方法论相关的部分。 随后，每个研究结果 f i f_{i} 被分解为一组原子性论断 A i = { a i ​ j } j = 1 n i A_{i}=\{a_{ij}\}_{j=1}^{n_{i}}。 一个原子性论断涉及一个具体的数值或定性目标，而一个研究结果可能包含多个原子性论断。 例如，“在患有乳腺腺样囊性癌的女性中，诊断时的平均年龄为 63 岁，中位数为 62 岁，年龄范围为 33–97 岁”是一个研究结果，而其中的各个目标，如“在患有乳腺腺样囊性癌的女性中，诊断时的平均年龄为 63 岁”（以及类似的“中位年龄：62 岁”和“年龄范围：33–97 岁”），各自成为一个独立的原子性论断。

paragraphs.en: Our first method asks whether an independent analysis of the same research question would reach a conclusion that contradicts the original paper (Figure 2 (A)). For each paper p p , a coding agent receives a research question specifying the topic and scope derived from p p , together with access to relevant data and additional documentation about the data, if available, and is tasked with independently answering the research question. The agent chooses its analytical approach, writes and executes code, and produces a research report r r . We then judge whether the conclusions in r r contradict those in p p . Appendix C documents the report-generation setup and the prompts for all 20 research questions.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的第一种方法会考察：如果独立分析同一研究问题，其结论是否与原始论文相矛盾（图 2 (A)）。 对于每篇论文 p p，一个编码智能体会收到一个源自 p p 的研究问题，该问题明确了主题和范围；同时，它还能访问相关数据以及（如有）关于这些数据的其他文档，并被要求独立回答该研究问题。 该智能体自行选择分析方法，编写并执行代码，然后生成一份研究报告 r r。 接着，我们会判断 r r 中的结论是否与 p p 中的结论相矛盾。 附录 C 记录了报告生成配置以及全部 20 个研究问题的提示词。

paragraphs.en: Fragmented data and documentation. Epidemiological studies often rely on external population data and relevant manuals. We curate these resources manually through an iterative process with expert input. Missing inputs often become apparent only as individual analyses are reconstructed, and identifying what is missing can itself require tracing the analysis step by step. For example, reproducing an incidence rate requires identifying an appropriate population denominator, locating its source, and checking that its geographic coverage, calendar years, and demographic definitions match the cancer records. Selecting among candidate sources also requires assessing their suitability and consulting the relevant manuals. This process therefore requires manual curation and expert judgment, rather than simply retrieving a known list of files.
paragraphs.zh: 零散的数据和文档。 流行病学研究通常依赖外部人口数据和相关手册。 我们通过与专家协作的迭代流程，手动整理这些资源。 缺失的输入往往只有在重建单个分析时才会显现出来，而要确定缺失了什么，本身就需要逐步追溯分析过程。 例如，要重现发病率，需要确定合适的人口分母、找到其来源，并核实其地理覆盖范围、年份和人口统计定义是否与癌症记录一致。 在候选来源中进行选择，还需要评估它们的适用性并查阅相关手册。 因此，这一过程需要人工整理和专家判断，而不仅仅是简单地检索一个已知的文件列表。

paragraphs.en: For each paper, we independently ask Opus 4.8 max via Claude Code and GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh via Codex to generate a report. GPT-5.6 Sol then compares each of the 40 reports with its corresponding paper for contradictions on their shared research question (Prompt 1 ). paragraphs.en: One coauthor with medical expertise and familiarity with SEER data manually examined 10 cases scored 7–9 in depth (five each from Perturbation Agent and Direct Coding Agent Analysis). Among the 5 cases from the Perturbation Agent, 2 suggested consequential changes, but closer expert scrutiny indicated that the alternatives were likely less defensible than the original analytical choices; the remaining 3 offered only limited qualifications to the papers’ conclusions. Among the 5 cases from direct coding agent analysis, 4 likewise offered only limited qualifications. The remaining 1 case identified a potentially overstated comparison between nasal and non-nasal incidence trends, but determining its consequence requires closer manuscript review and statistical consultation. Thus, 9 cases did not establish a consequential change under a defensible alternative, while 1 remains flagged for further review. Table 4 illustrates 3 cases with one from each category: a likely less defensible alternative, a limited qualification to the paper’s conclusions, and a potentially consequential issue requiring further review.

paragraphs.en: Overall, our pipeline narrows the material requiring expert attention by autonomously reconstructing published findings, executing alternative analyses, and prioritizing potentially consequential results. Across 579 fully reproduced findings, it identifies 55 with model-assessed consequential links, providing a focused shortlist and supporting evidence for expert review. Experts can therefore concentrate on whether the flagged alternatives are scientifically defensible and will materially change the conclusions, rather than reconstructing and testing each analysis from scratch manually.
paragraphs.zh: 总体而言，我们的流程通过自主重建已发表的发现、执行替代性分析并优先处理可能具有重大影响的结果，从而减少了需要专家关注的内容。 在 579 项完全复现的发现中，该流程识别出 55 项经模型评估具有重大关联性的发现，为专家审查提供了重点候选列表和相关证据。 因此，专家可以专注于判断这些被标记的替代方案是否具有科学上的合理性，以及它们是否会对结论产生实质性影响，而无需手动从头重建和测试每一项分析。

paragraphs.en: We introduced SEER-Repro, a benchmark of 20 published SEER studies, and an AI-assisted pipeline for evaluating reproducibility and robustness to analytical choices. Our reproduction agent recovered 77.4% of atomic claims. Automated robustness assessments then prioritized 55 of 579 fully reproduced findings (9.5%) for expert review, providing a focused shortlist with supporting analytical evidence. Expert examination of 10 flagged cases clarified why 9 did not establish consequential changes under defensible alternatives and identified 1 potentially consequential issue requiring further investigation. These results illustrate how automated analysis can focus expert attention on questions that warrant closer scientific scrutiny.
paragraphs.zh: 我们推出了 SEER-Repro，这是一个包含 20 项已发表 SEER 研究的基准测试，以及一条由人工智能辅助的流程，用于评估可重复性以及对分析选择的稳健性。 我们的可重复性智能体恢复了 77.4% 的原子性主张。 随后，自动稳健性评估从 579 项完全可重复的发现中优先挑选出 55 项（9.5%）进行专家审查，从而提供了一个附有支持性分析证据的聚焦候选清单。 对 10 个被标记案例的专家审查阐明了为何其中 9 个在可辩护的替代方案下未能确立具有后果性的变化，并识别出 1 个可能需要进一步调查的潜在后果性问题。 这些结果表明，自动化分析如何将专家的注意力集中在需要更严格科学审视的问题上。

paragraphs.en: SEER provides an early, high-stakes testbed for this approach. Longer term, such checks could become part of scientific infrastructure: published findings could be routinely reassessed as data, methods, and analytical alternatives evolve, with potentially consequential sensitivities prioritized for expert review.

paragraphs.en: This work aims to support scientific reliability by evaluating the reproducibility and analytical robustness of published cancer epidemiology findings. We acknowledge that errors in our pipeline, including but not limited to data selection, LLM-generated code, interpretation, and grading, may lead to incorrect assessments. Failure to reproduce a finding may also reflect unavailable historical data (as documented in Section 4.1 ). Sensitivity to an alternative analysis does not invalidate the original study and requires careful expert judgment to assess its significance (as discussed in Section 4 ). Our goal is to help experts identify findings that warrant closer examination, making rigorous scientific review more accessible while keeping expert judgment central to the process.
paragraphs.zh: 本研究旨在通过评估已发表癌症流行病学研究结果的可重复性和分析稳健性，来支持其科学可靠性。 我们承认，我们流程中的错误（包括但不限于数据选择、大型语言模型生成的代码、解释和评分）可能导致错误的评估。 无法复现某项研究结果也可能反映出历史数据不可用（如第 4.1 节所述）。 对替代分析方法的敏感性并不否定原始研究的结论，需要专家谨慎判断其重要性（如第 4 节所讨论）。 我们的目标是帮助专家识别出需要进一步仔细审查的研究结果，使严谨的科学评审更容易实施，同时确保专家判断在整个过程中处于核心地位。

paragraphs.en: SEER 9, SEER 13, and SEER 18 identify different geographic cohorts, with standard diagnosis-year coverage beginning in 1975, 1992, and 2000, respectively. Figure 4 summarizes their expansion and subsequent changes. With the November 2021 submission, released in April 2022, Detroit was excluded from the new databases, yielding SEER 8, 12, and 17. Massachusetts was subsequently excluded from the November 2024 submission, changing SEER 22 to SEER 21 ( National Cancer Institute, 2026c ; National Cancer Institute, 2026b ) .
paragraphs.zh: SEER 9、SEER 13 和 SEER 18 分别识别了不同的地理队列，其标准诊断年份覆盖范围始于 1975 年、1992 年和 2000 年。 图 4 总结了它们的扩展及后续变化。 随着 2021 年 11 月的提交数据（于 2022 年 4 月发布），底特律被排除在新数据库之外，从而形成了 SEER 8、SEER 12 和 SEER 17。 随后，马萨诸塞州在 2024 年 11 月的提交数据中被排除在外，导致 SEER 22 变为 SEER 21（美国国家癌症研究所，2026c；美国国家癌症研究所，2026b）。

paragraphs.en: The supplemental November 2020 database preserves SEER 9 records, including Detroit, through 2018. We use this retained cohort and select papers whose analyses do not require additional registries. It is in general difficult to reconstruct historical SEER 13 and SEER 18 datasets using the newer, Detroit-excluding releases (SEER 12 and SEER 17), since each case does not record the exact associated registry.

paragraphs.en: Retaining the registry grouping does not guarantee identical historical inputs. For example, the November 2020 submission changed the default malignant-behavior definition and excluded approximately 10,000 previously included, no-longer-reportable borderline cases, predominantly ovarian tumors ( National Cancer Institute, 2026a ) . Our local failure diagnostics also identify unavailable radiation-treatment fields, preventing reconstruction of some treatment proportions even when registry coverage matches. We retain these limitations when interpreting claim-level reproduction outcomes. For instance, these cases would count towards “Data Issues” in Table 2 .
paragraphs.zh: 保留登记册分组并不保证历史输入完全相同。 例如，2020年11月的提交版本修改了默认恶性行为定义，并排除了约10,000个此前被纳入但现已无法报告的边缘病例，其中主要是卵巢肿瘤（美国国家癌症研究所，2026a）。 我们的局部失败诊断还能识别出不可用的放射治疗野，即使登记册覆盖范围一致，这也导致部分治疗比例无法重建。 在解释索赔层面的复现结果时，我们保留了这些局限性。 例如，这些病例将在表2中计入“数据问题”。

paragraphs.en: Select Analytical Choices (Step 1). For each published paper p p , we identify candidate analytical choices relevant to its fully reproduced findings F p rep F^{\mathrm{rep}}_{p} . An LLM receives the paper, eligible findings, and reproduction evidence E p E_{p} , and extracts choices such as cohort definitions, endpoints, subgroup definitions, statistical models, and interpretation rules (Prompt 7 ). For each generated report r ∈ ℛ p r\in\mathcal{R}_{p} , a separate call extracts choices from the report and its available execution log, linking them to the paper’s eligible findings where applicable (Prompt 8 ). We verify finding identifiers and supporting quotations, attempt to repair invalid candidates (Prompt 9 ), and remove evidence or candidates that remain ungrounded. The validated candidates from all sources are then pooled: an LLM merges descriptions of the same scientific decision and ranks the resulting choices by scientific importance, uncertainty, feasibility, and redundancy, selecting at most 20 choices before any alternative analysis is run (Prompt 10 ). Review and repair calls resolve problems with the proposed selection (Prompts 11 – 15 ), yielding the finalized choice set 𝒞 p \mathcal{C}_{p} used to propose alternatives.

paragraphs.en: Propose Alternatives. (Step 2 of the Perturbation Agent in Figure 2 ) For each selected analytical choice, an LLM examines how each paper or report implements that choice, using the source text and available execution evidence (Prompt 16 ) and documents the exact setting. Invalid plans are repaired against the validation errors, with deterministic checks of identifiers and comparison coverage (Prompt 23 ). Executable comparisons are then fed to coding agents for implementation (Prompt 24 ). The executor first runs the baseline unchanged and checks it against the frozen validation criteria. It then copies the baseline, changes only the specified choice and its listed dependent calculations, and saves the baseline output, alternative output, validation evidence, and exact code diff. paragraphs.en: The pipeline prepares the SEER-Repro environment for execution. The launch prompt (Prompt 28 ) directs the coding agent to follow the execution instructions (Prompt 24 ). The agent recovers the baseline implementation from preserved code, structured execution traces, or legacy transcripts, in that order of preference; it constructs a fresh implementation only when no prior implementation evidence survives. It then validates the unchanged baseline, executes the specified alternatives, and saves the results and supporting evidence. If a Codex session ends successfully without the required results file, a continuation prompt asks it to finish using the same workspace (Prompt 26 ). If the file remains missing, a final prompt stops further analysis and requires it to record existing results, marking unfinished comparisons as unavailable (Prompt 27 ).
paragraphs.zh: 该流程为执行准备 SEER-Repro 环境。 启动提示（提示 28）指导编码智能体遵循执行指令（提示 24）。 智能体按优先顺序从保留的代码、结构化的执行痕迹或旧版转录记录中恢复基线实现；仅当没有任何先前实现的证据留存时，才会构建全新的实现。 接着，它验证未更改的基线，执行指定的替代方案，并保存结果及支持性证据。 如果 Codex 会话成功结束但缺少所需的结果文件，则通过延续提示要求其使用相同的工作区完成操作（提示 26）。 如果该文件仍然缺失，则最终提示将停止进一步分析，并要求其记录现有结果，同时将未完成的部分标记为不可用（提示 27）。

paragraphs.en: Inputs and unit of assessment. One judge call receives the reproduction report for an original finding together with its atomic targets. Each target includes its identifier, claim text, reference answer, numerical or semantic evaluation mode, verification target, source quotation, and required analytical assumptions. The judge is instructed to assess every atomic target independently: reproducing one component of a finding does not establish that its other components were reproduced. The grading call receives the report and structured targets, rather than independently inspecting the complete code and execution trace or rerunning the analysis.
paragraphs.zh: 输入与评估单位。 一次判评调用会收到原始发现结果的复现报告及其原子目标。 每个目标均包含其标识符、主张文本、参考答案、数值或语义评估模式、验证目标、来源引文以及所需的分析假设。 判评系统被要求独立评估每个原子目标：复现一个发现结果的部分内容，并不等同于证明了其其他部分也被成功复现。 评分调用会收到报告与结构化目标，而非独立检查完整的代码和执行轨迹，或重新运行分析。

paragraphs.en: Method validity. The judge assesses whether the reported computation uses a valid method for the specific target. This includes compatibility with required cohort bounds, disease and variable coding, outcome measures, grouping, denominators, standardization conventions, temporal data definitions, and statistical-model settings. A conflicting analytical assumption makes the method invalid; insufficient methodological evidence makes it unclear. The report need not repeat every required assumption verbatim, but it must establish a compatible computation. Both invalid and unclear methods lead to a not-reproduced verdict, even when the extracted numerical value matches the reference.
